In this guide, we compare leading budgeting and forecasting software on features, pricing, and integrations so you can find the option that fits your finance stack and growth stage

## How we chose the best budgeting and forecasting software‡


In this list, we evaluated business budgeting software and forecasting platforms based on:

- Scalability and usability. Support for growing teams, multi-entity structures, and both finance and non-finance users.

- Fit for different business types. From small businesses that need day-to-day spend control to larger, multi-entity organizations running complex FP&A processes.

## Key questions about budgeting and forecasting software


### What is budgeting and forecasting software?


Budgeting and forecasting software helps businesses plan how money will be spent and predict how the business will perform financially. On the budgeting side, that means setting spending limits by department, project, or card and tracking actuals against those limits. On the forecasting side, it means modeling future revenue, expenses, and cash flow based on historical data, business drivers, and assumptions.


The scope varies widely across this category. Some platforms, like[BILL Spend & Expense](https://www.bill.com/product/spend-and-expense) , focus on operational budgeting — tying budgets directly to[company cards and expense controls](https://www.bill.com/product/corporate-cards) so overspending is caught at the point of purchase. Others, like Anaplan, Workday Adaptive Planning, Vena, and Planful, focus on FP&A (financial planning and analysis) — building driver-based models, running what-if scenarios, and consolidating plans across departments or entities.


### How does budgeting and forecasting software work?


1. **Set up budgets or planning models.** Teams define budgets by department, project, or card, or build financial models with revenue and expense drivers.
2. **Connect data sources.** Most platforms sync with accounting software, ERPs, HRIS platforms, or card transactions to keep budgets and forecasts current.
3. **Track actuals against plan.** As money is spent or revenue comes in, the software compares actuals to budget or forecast and flags variances.
4. **Model scenarios.** Many forecasting platforms let finance teams run what-if scenarios to see how changes in assumptions affect outcomes.
5. **Report and adjust.** Dashboards and reports give finance leaders and department heads visibility into performance, so budgets and forecasts can be updated as conditions change.


### What features should you look for in business budgeting software?


- **Real-time spend visibility.** For operational budgeting, look for software that shows spending as it happens rather than after the fact, like BILL Spend & Expense's real-time expense tracking. \[1\]
- **Scenario and what-if modeling.** For FP&A-focused platforms, look for the ability to model multiple scenarios and quickly compare outcomes, a capability offered by Anaplan, Workday Adaptive Planning, Vena, and Planful. \[4\]\[7\]\[10\]\[14\]
- **Driver-based forecasting.** Forecasts tied to real business drivers (revenue, headcount, costs) tend to be more actionable than static, historical-only projections. \[6\]\[7\]\[10\]
- **Integration with your accounting system or ERP.** Whether it's a two-way sync with QuickBooks and NetSuite or connections to any ERP or GL, integrations reduce manual data entry and keep numbers current. \[1\]\[8\]
- **Budget enforcement, not just tracking.** Some platforms only report on budget variance after the fact; others, like BILL, tie budgets directly to card limits so spending is controlled in real time. \[1\]
- **Collaboration and approval workflows.** Look for tools that let budget owners submit inputs, track approvals, and see roll-ups without relying on email chains or disconnected spreadsheets. \[10\]


### How much does budgeting and forecasting software cost?


Pricing across this category is largely custom and quote-based:


- BILL Spend & Expense doesn't publish set pricing — it's based on business needs and number of users, and you can request a demo for a personalized plan. \[1\]
- Anaplan doesn't publish pricing on its planning, FP&A, or datasheet pages — pricing is available by requesting a demo. \[4\]\[5\]\[6\]
- Workday Adaptive Planning lists pricing as "varies" for both its core planning product and its Close & Consolidation package, with a free 30-day trial available. \[8\]
- Vena offers two tiers, Professional and Complete, but doesn't publish dollar figures — both require a demo request for pricing. \[11\]
- Planful doesn't publish pricing on its solution hub or finance pages — contact Planful directly for a quote. \[13\]\[14\]


Because so much of this category is quote-based, the real cost differences often come down to what's included at each tier — for example, whether AI features, sandbox environments, or premium support require an upgraded plan — rather than a simple sticker price.


## Benefits of budgeting and forecasting software


Real-time control over spending. Tying budgets directly to card limits and approval workflows — as BILL Spend & Expense does — means overspending can be caught before a purchase happens rather than during a month-end review. \[1\]


Faster planning cycles. Anaplan reports that its platform can increase finance team productivity by up to 40% by streamlining planning on a single platform, while Vena reports helping finance teams achieve 66% faster planning cycles. \[4\]\[12\]


More accurate forecasts. Driver-based models that update with real-time data — rather than static, spreadsheet-only projections — help teams catch variances and adjust forecasts as conditions change, according to Vena and Workday Adaptive Planning. \[7\]\[10\]


Less manual, spreadsheet-only work. Anaplan's own materials describe eliminating dependence on spreadsheets and IT for planning, while Vena and Planful both emphasize reducing manual data prep through automated integrations. \[6\]\[12\]\[13\]


Better cross-team collaboration. Platforms like Anaplan and Vena support connected plans across finance, sales, operations, and HR, with roll-ups and approval workflows that keep budget owners aligned. \[6\]\[10\]


## How to choose the right budget planning software for your business


Factor How it affects your decision


What “budgeting” means for your team If you need day-to-day spend control tied to company cards, prioritize platforms built around real-time budget enforcement. If you need multi-year financial models and scenario planning, prioritize dedicated FP&A platforms.


Company size and complexity Larger, multi-entity organizations tend to need the connected planning and consolidation features found in enterprise FP&A platforms, while smaller businesses may only need operational budgeting tied to spend.


Excel and spreadsheet attachment If your finance team has deep institutional knowledge built into Excel models, an Excel-native platform can reduce the change management required to adopt new software.


Integration requirements Check whether a platform offers a native two-way sync with your accounting software or ERP, not just CSV import/export — the depth of integration affects how current your numbers stay.


Forecasting depth If you need driver-based forecasts, rolling forecasts, or what-if scenario modeling, confirm the platform supports those specific methods rather than basic budget-vs-actual reporting.


Pricing model Since most budgeting and forecasting software in this category is quote-based, ask each provider what’s included at each tier so you can compare total cost, not just a starting price.


## Conclusion


For small and midsize businesses that want business budgeting software to mean real control — not just a report after the money's already spent — BILL Spend & Expense and the BILL Divvy Card tie custom budgets directly to company cards, add credit lines from $1000-5M,¹ and use AI to capture and categorize every transaction automatically. \[1\]\[2\]


It's a different approach than the enterprise FP&A platforms on this list, which focus on complex financial modeling and scenario planning, but for businesses that want budgets enforced in real time alongside the credit and expense tools to support their growth, BILL offers that combination on one platform. \[1\]\[2\]\[3\]
